hypothesis: The extra full round after the first checkpoint claim is mostly dead time for a family game: the claimant already has a complete set, and median city phase is 18 rounds. Ending the city phase at the close of the claim round should shorten games by about one round while the collection race keeps its decisions, because players who want to finish sets must plan to be near their last districts before the claim, not after it.
prediction: Median rounds fall by about one on both suites; transition equipment of non-claimants falls by at most half an item on average; draws, cancellations, contest availability, and the winning profiles stay near baseline; the first challenger's win share rises by at most five points.
refutation_evidence: Median rounds do not fall; or non-claimant transition equipment collapses (the round carried real catch-up decisions); or the first challenger's share rises past baseline plus five points (the head start grows); or any mechanical or counterplay gate fails.
